readings: Match each transaction record to its trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match) and drop records with no matching trader. Then, for each trader type (`tradekind`), count the distinct traders (`trdref`) who have at least one matched transaction record. Count each trader once, however many records they have. Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
queries:
WITH per_type AS (
  SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.trdref) AS cnt
  FROM transactionrecord tr
  JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
  GROUP BY t.tradekind
),
stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt
  FROM per_type
)
SELECT p.tradekind,
       p.cnt,
       p.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt,
       p.cnt - s.avg_cnt
FROM per_type p
CROSS JOIN stats s
WHERE s.avg_cnt IS NOT NULL
  AND p.cnt > s.avg_cnt;
